basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 19.' and it opens 'VERS. 19.-- Formatis igitur de humo cunctis animantibus terrae, adduxit ea ad Adam.'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 19.-- Formatis igitur de humo cunctis animantibus terrae, adduxit ea ad Adam. Sciendum | est non circuitu locali adducens, sicut aucupes et venatores, sed occulto nutu suae potentiae voluit ut venirent, ut videret quid vocaret ea. Videret, id est discerneret et intelligeret quid vocaret ea.
